findings.mathematical_substance: I checked the hypothesis independently. (i) Every 1-subdivision of a simple graph G with an edge lies in C_2: subdivision vertices form the side of degree exactly two, and a 4-cycle would correspond to a double edge of G, excluded by simplicity; cycles of length 2k correspond to k-cycles of G, so girth is at least six. (ii) For H in C_2 with bipartition (X,Y), deleting the X-vertices of degree at most one and then isolated vertices leaves X-vertices of degree exactly two with distinct neighbour pairs (equal pairs would close a 4-cycle), i.e. the 1-subdivision of a simple graph on Y, possibly edgeless. (iii) Pendant-vertex removal through the finite lemmas: with p=2e(G)/n^2 and d=np, on a host of maximum degree at most 2d, hom(H',G) ≥ hom(H,G)/Δ(G) ≥ ½ n^{v(H')} p^{e(H')} (deleting direction), and with Lemma 3.4 of CKLL a subgraph G' on at least n/64 vertices with minimum degree at least d/4 gives hom(H,G) ≥ δ(G')·hom(H',G') ≥ (np/4)(n/64)^{v(H')}(p/4)^{e(H')} (adding direction); Lemma 3.3 then yields the Sidorenko property with constants depending only on H. Both directions therefore follow from the fully proved finite lemmas without the sketched symmetric regular reduction (Coregliano–Razborov Theorem 8.2). Note that the class equivalence itself needs only the adding direction (⇐ uses it, ⇒ is direct from (i)); the deleting direction is extra and must be proved if asserted. The argument is elementary but correct as sketched; the deliverable must supply it in full.
findings.necessity: The reduction is not necessary for deciding the root, and the proposal says so (contribution.necessity null; 'the reduction settles nothing by itself'). Its value is structural: it identifies the C_2 branch with a named open problem, so a counterexample inside C_2 is essentially a 1-subdivision and any proof on C_2 must settle Problem 1.5, which CKLL call outside the reach of current methods. This is a legitimate, modest clarification; it should not be read as progress toward closure.

findings.root_connection: The node targets the premise on-c2 of the proposed route c2-split, whose conclusion is the root obligation obligation-000001 (contract digest 1cbe81a8…, claim digest 43d81023…). The route splits the girth-six bipartite graphs with an edge into C_2 (some bipartition has one side of maximum degree at most two) and its complement (each side of every bipartition has a vertex of degree at least three); the bridge c2-case-split is a tautological case distinction, so the decomposition is logically faithful to the root statement. The split is exhaustive because membership in C_2 is an existential condition over bipartitions and its negation is exactly the stated complement. A refutation of either premise also decides the root negatively, so the route does not lose the negative branch of the requested decision.
findings.scope: Claim scope: every H in C_2 and every graphon W; equivalently finite simple hosts counting all homomorphisms. The node is nonclosing: it proves an equivalence with Problem 1.5 of CKLL (1-subdivision of every graph), not the premise itself. The deliverable must handle the degenerate case where the reduced core is edgeless (H a star forest plus isolated vertices), where the equivalence is trivial, and must state Problem 1.5 for simple graphs so that the image of the reduction is exactly the problem's domain (every simple base graph with an edge arises by (i)). The complement premise outside-c2 and the bridge are untouched by this node.
findings.significance: Low-to-moderate and honestly stated. The node fixes the exact status of one half of the case split as an existing open problem, lets known positive cases (KNRS, regular-KNRS, Sidorenko base graphs) be read off for C_2, and interacts with the barrier node's observation that the counterexample's sign model is trivial on 4-cycle-free patterns. It does not move the root toward a decision by itself, and the budget (new account, retreat at 10 moves, no computation) is proportionate to an elementary proof write-up.

unresolved_objections.description: The deliverable must prove or precisely cite the tensor power trick used inside Lemma 3.3 (KLL Lemma 3.4 omits its proof, referring to Sidorenko's Remark 2), and must apply it after the reduction from bounded-degree to general hosts, since tensor powers do not preserve the maximum-to-average degree ratio.

The degenerate case in which the reduced core is edgeless (H a disjoint union of stars centred in Y plus isolated vertices) must be handled explicitly, and Problem 1.5 must be stated for simple graphs so that the image of the reduction is exactly its domain.

The graphon-to-finite-host equivalence (KLL (1.1)–(1.2)) must be stated with its citation in the proof; and if the deleting direction of pendant removal (H Sidorenko ⇒ H minus pendant vertex Sidorenko) is asserted, it must be proved, although only the adding direction is needed for the class equivalence.

Semantic Scholar was unavailable to all study queries and Fox–Wei 2017 was not read in full; these are recorded gaps of the novelty record and would bear on any later openness or closure claim, not on this reduction.
